summary: Aspiring business owners often fail because they **fixate on massive corporate empires** like those built by tech legends instead of focusing on immediate, practical ventures. Traditional schooling compounds this issue by rewarding **strict rule-following and individual compliance**, which leaves people entirely unprepared for the real-world demands of **delegation and persuasion**. Ultimately, true entrepreneurial success requires embracing **scrappy, hands-on opportunities** and mastering the art of sales, skills that are rarely taught in standard classrooms and must be cultivated through experience.
